question: Review a consumer integration targeting the current development ResponseLimits contract documented at https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo-Fabric/blob/main/docs/sdk/results-and-errors.mdx#response-and-artifact-limits. The preinstalled 0.7.0a20261117 nightly predates this API, so this task requests a Python code proposal and failure-handling explanation only, not execution. Show explicit response and screenshot-artifact budgets, explain omitted local versus OpenShell limits, and handle a budget breach after the agent has acted without replaying side effects. Do not install or invoke an older SDK as if it implemented the new contract.
ground_truth: Use public ResponseLimits on RuntimeConfig.response_limits. Local omission or None preserves unbudgeted local results, whereas OpenShell keeps default transfer budgets. An empty limits object opts into default budgets locally. For a larger image raise both max_artifact_file_bytes and max_artifact_bytes, return the complete image as a declared artifact instead of base64 output, and keep the normalized result within max_response_bytes. Limits need no adapter capability declaration. A breach returns failed/response_limit_exceeded and clears output, artifact references, adapter metadata and events while preserving usage, execution evidence, telemetry, system stats and resource snapshots. It does not roll back side effects or justify automatic retry. Budgets do not limit streaming chunks already delivered, sandbox memory, or the separate collection deadline. The supplied starter files and preinstalled dependencies are sufficient for this bounded exercise. Judge the concrete implementation or code/design proposal requested by the prompt; no live model, real harness deployment, or package publication is required.
expected_behavior: Uses public ResponseLimits through runtime.response_limits
Distinguishes omitted local limits, default OpenShell budgets, and an empty limits object
Raises both per-file and aggregate artifact budgets for a larger screenshot
Returns an artifact instead of inline base64 and checks the result response budget
Handles failed status and response_limit_exceeded without silently truncating or retrying
Preserves retained execution evidence while recognizing that rejected payload fields are cleared
Does not claim rollback, adapter capability requirements, or limits on delivered stream chunks
